narrative.summary: Lesotho governs AI mainly through the Artificial Intelligence Policy of the Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation (MICSTI), finalised in August 2026, which builds on the 2024 National Digital Transformation Strategy. The policy leaves AI oversight to existing sector regulators and plans AI legislation and a regulatory sandbox. The only binding rule is in the Data Protection Act 2011, which regulates decisions based solely on automated processing. There is no AI law, and a National AI Strategy is being prepared.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation (MICSTI)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents on the government portal and the official Gazette. The Data Protection Act was read from a scanned Gazette copy. No website was found for the Data Protection Commission, and the National AI Strategy and National Digital Policy are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Final version posted on the Government of Lesotho portal (National Policies) on 17 August 2026; the document cover is dated 2025 and its foreword is signed by Minister Nthati Moorosi. Published together with the Data Management Policy and the Broadband and Shared Infrastructure Policy. It runs to 2030, when the policy and implementation plan are to be refreshed; a National AI Strategy to operationalise it was being developed in 2026 (see leads).
instruments.summary: Lesotho's first national AI policy, prepared by MICSTI with UNDP support, setting eight focus areas: AI leadership and governance, legislation and compliance, capacity building, AI infrastructure, productivity and jobs, inclusive and ethical AI, SDG-related services, and international alignment. It chooses a decentralised approach in which existing sectoral regulators (Central Bank, Lesotho Communications Authority, Consumer Protection Authority, Competition Commission, data protection body) oversee AI in their domains, with MICSTI as policymaker, the Chief Digital Officer and a Digital Government Implementation Agency as coordinator/regulator, and a Data and AI Sub-Committee as advisory platform. Its implementation plan to 2030 provides for AI-specific legislation, updates to data-protection and consumer laws, and an AI regulatory sandbox.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Lesotho's primary AI governance instrument; defines institutional roles and the planned legislative path for AI.

instruments.summary: Lesotho's national digital transformation strategy to 2030, organised in five pillars: enabling environment (leadership, institutions, policies and legislation), digital government, digital infrastructure, digital population and digital business. Under the enabling-environment pillar it commits the government to develop data and transformative-technology (AI) policies and data-sharing rules, and it identifies AI, big data and IoT skills gaps. It sets the Chief Digital Officer function and a Whole-of-Society Advisory Council later used by the AI Policy for its Data and AI Sub-Committee.

instruments.current_status: Published as Act No. 5 of 2012 in Government Gazette Vol. 57 No. 19 of 22 February 2012; s. 1 provides it comes into operation on publication in the Gazette. The full text used is the gazette scan hosted by the Central Bank of Lesotho on its legislation page. The AI Policy (2025/2026) calls for it to be updated with AI-related provisions.
instruments.summary: Lesotho's data protection law, establishing a Data Protection Commission and principles for processing personal information (minimality, purpose limitation, security, data subject access and correction, sensitive-data rules, cross-border transfer limits, notification of processing). Section 51 provides that a person may not be subjected to a decision with legal or significant effect based solely on automated processing of personal information intended to profile aspects of personality or personal habits, subject to exceptions such as decisions in connection with a contract. Enforcement is through Commission investigations, enforcement notices and civil remedies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law with an explicit automated decision-making rule (s. 51) that applies to AI profiling.

organizations.ai_governance_role: Lead ministry for AI and digital policy (MICSTI). Issued the Artificial Intelligence Policy (final version posted 17 August 2026) and the National Digital Transformation Strategy: Agenda 2030; under the AI Policy it is the AI policymaker, with the Chief Digital Officer leading the national AI agenda and a Digital Government Implementation Agency planned as coordinator/regulator.

organizations.ai_governance_role: Enacted the Data Protection Act, 2011 (Act No. 5 of 2012), which includes a right not to be subject to solely automated decisions (s. 51). No AI bill found on the National Assembly website.
